title: Interventions for Complex Traumatic Events (INCiTE): Systematic Review
author: Peter Coventry
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdbni2me

steps.title: Conduct Literature Searches
steps.instruction: Perform comprehensive searches to identify relevant studies for both effectiveness and acceptability syntheses.

substeps.instruction: Search electronic databases including MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Science Citation Index, International Pharmaceutical Abstracts, and PILOTS.

Conduct journal hand searches, reference list searches, targeted author searches, grey literature searches (including service user-led organization material), research register searches, and forward citation searching.

Run a separate search for qualitative evidence using terms relating to qualitative designs and user experience of therapies, developed via previous meta-syntheses, MEDLINE MeSH thesaurus, and team discussion.
Flag qualitative process evaluations associated with clinical trials during the effectiveness screening process.

steps.title: Screen Studies for Eligibility
steps.instruction: Filter identified studies based on pre-defined inclusion and exclusion criteria using a two-reviewer process.

substeps.instruction: Independently screen titles and abstracts; retrieve full-text articles if both reviewers agree or if there is disagreement.

Independently assess full-text articles against inclusion criteria: Adults (18+) exposed to complex interpersonal trauma (e.g., childhood abuse, domestic violence, refugees, torture survivors, human trafficking).
Exclude participants with only single, non-interpersonal traumatic events (e.g., road traffic accidents, natural disasters).
Include mixed population studies if ≥75% of participants have complex trauma, or if data for the complex trauma sub-group is presented separately.
Resolve any remaining disagreements through discussion with other team members.
Record all inclusions and exclusions for PRISMA flow chart and characteristics tables.

steps.title: Extract Study Data
steps.instruction: Systematically extract technical and clinical data from included studies using a pre-specified extraction sheet.

substeps.instruction: Extract data regarding study sample, setting, methods, intervention, control, and reported outcome measures.
Categorize data by timeframes: short-term (post-treatment to 6 months), long-term (7-12 months), and very long-term (>12 months).
Perform extraction by one reviewer and independently check by a second reviewer, resolving discrepancies via original studies or a third reviewer.

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias and Quality
steps.instruction: Evaluate the methodological quality of included studies using tool-specific frameworks.

substeps.instruction: Assess RCTs using the Cochrane Collaboration Risk of Bias (RoB) tool.
Assess non-randomised studies using the Cochrane Risk of Bias for Non-Randomised Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I).
Assess qualitative studies using the CASP checklist and the CerQual approach for coherence and methodological limitations.
Perform assessments by one reviewer and independently check by a second, resolving discrepancies via a third reviewer if necessary.

steps.title: Synthesize Quantitative Data
steps.instruction: Perform meta-analyses and network meta-analyses to determine clinical effectiveness.

substeps.instruction: Pool data for similar interventions, populations, and contexts, exploring heterogeneity using I-squared.
Adjust cluster trials by calculating the 'design effect' to reduce effective sample size.
Handle multiple treatment groups by analyzing pair-wise comparisons and dividing shared groups evenly to avoid double counting.
Select a single outcome measure per category based on a comparability decision rule or take the median.
Apply standardized mean difference and back-transform to mean differences or number needed to treat (NNT) where assumptions are met.
Conduct network meta-analyses for psychological interventions using a Bayesian approach (WinBUGS) following ISPOR and NICE Technical Support Document 2 guidelines.
Perform subgroup meta-analyses for victims of sexual abuse (child/adult), refugees/asylum seekers, and trafficking/exploitation.

steps.title: Synthesize Qualitative Data
steps.instruction: Perform a narrative synthesis of qualitative evidence regarding acceptability and feasibility.

substeps.instruction: Apply a narrative synthesis approach, prioritizing studies with 'thicker' data descriptions (rigorous collection/analysis) over 'thinner' descriptions.
Summarize the impact of methodological limitations and certainty using the CerQual approach.
Integrate findings by mapping qualitative themes onto quantitative acceptability ratings for intervention uptake.
